 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Brandon Miller had six points (2-of-14 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, two steals, one block and one three-pointer against the Hawks on Friday. 
 There’s no sugarcoating it; Miller is off to a rough start to begin the season. The 23-year-old small forward had 18 points in the opener, but shot just 7-of-21 from the floor. He followed that performance up by going 2-of-14, including 1-of-11 from behind the three-point line. He’s now 4-of-25 (16 percent) from behind the arc to begin the season. Miller was an almost incomprehensible -37 in 22 minutes in the 128-81 loss to the Haws Friday. Is this rock bottom? Because it feels like it can only get better from here. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Brandon Miller had 18 points (7-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and three three-pointers agains the Nets on Wednesday. 
 Miller had 18 points, but struggled with efficiency as he was 7-of-21 from the field and 3-of-14 from behind the three-point line. There will be better games in his future, but with Kon Knueppel and Coby White sidelined defenses will be continue to key on Miller.

 Charlotte Hornets start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate in season opener against the Nets 
 The Hornets have Kon Knueppel and Coby White out, so Schroeder and now Sion James will get the start with Grayson Allen coming off the bench. Even in a start, Sion James is not a great per minute producer and will likely not impact many fantasy leagues even in a start. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Hornets and Brandon Miller have agreed to a five-year, $209 million extension. 
 Miller’s future in Charlotte is set, as he’s agreed to a rookie-scale extension worth more than $40 million per year. With the offseason decision to trade LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, the franchise has moved forward with Miller and Kon Knueppel as cornerstones. Miller appeared in 65 games last season, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.0 steals and 3.1 three-pointers per game. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller recorded 18 points (6-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Sunday’s exhibition against the Bucks. 
 Miller was on the court on Sunday after sitting out Charlotte’s preseason opener. He led the Hornets in scoring, and he’ll be expected to do that nightly once the regular season begins. Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is not expected to be available when the season opens on October 21, which may raise Miller’s fantasy ceiling. However, to live up to those hopes, he’ll need to be more efficient. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will miss the preseason and be re-evaluated during the first week of the regular season. 
 Given how well Knueppel played as a rookie and the Hornets’ decision to move on from LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges, Friday’s news gives his 2026-27 season a brutal start. At a minimum, the runner-up for Rookie of the Year will be sidelined for four weeks, and that’s just for him to be re-evaluated. According to the Hornets, Knueppel suffered the left hamstring injury during an offseason on-court activity. His absence boosts the early-season values of Brandon Miller and Coby White while also making Grayson Allen a more viable late-round option in drafts. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller (shoulder) continues to progress in his recovery from offseason left shoulder surgery. 
 Miller, who missed 13 games early last season after suffering a subluxation of his left shoulder, underwent surgery in May to address instability in the area. While he still has not been fully cleared to resume basketball activities, the 6-foot-7 wing is making strides in his recovery. “It’s going good, going good,” Miller told the Charlotte Observer. “I’m getting stronger. That’s all I can ask for. The stronger I get, the more mobile I am with the shoulder and that is the most important thing.” With the Hornets moving on from LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges this summer, Miller’s role will expand next season, raising his fantasy ceiling. 
 LaMelo Ball 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #1 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that multiple teams have been “actively” making offers for Hornets point guard LaMelo Ball. 
 While the report says the Hornets have not signaled they’re looking to move on from Ball, that has not kept some teams from taking the initiative to see if they can get something done. According to both Charania and NBA insider Marc Stein, Minnesota and Toronto are the teams in question. Having struggled with injuries in recent years, Ball appeared in 72 games last season and was one of the reasons why the Hornets landed in the Play-In tournament. He averaged 20.1 points, 4.8 rebounds, 7.1 assists, 1.2 steals and 3.8 three-pointers per game, shooting 40.7 percent from the field and 89.9 percent from the foul line. If Ball is moved, it would be a clear sign that Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel are the Hornets’ cornerstones.

 Brandon Miller underwent surgery to address left shoulder instability. 
 Miller is out indefinitely, but expected to make a full recovery. He hurt his shoulder early in the season, but managed to play 65 games while wearing a wrap on his shoulder most of the time. Miller led the Hornets with 20.2 points per game this season. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller totaled 14 points (5-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, one assist, two steals and four three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Magic. 
 Miller shot the ball efficiently and had a great three-point shooting performance on Friday. However, he was responsible for five of Charlotte’s 16 turnovers, and was just one of several Hornets to find difficulty on the offensive end. A blowout loss ultimately limited Miller to 29 minutes in the season-ending loss. Nonetheless, he put together another solid fantasy season in Year 3. Perhaps a jump could come in his fourth season. 
 Brandon Miller 
 CHA 
 Forward 
 #24 
 Brandon Miller added 23 points (9-of-17 FGs), five rebounds, five assists, two blocks and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Heat. 
 In his first taste of the postseason, Miller delivered a well-rounded performance to help Charlotte keep its playoff hopes alive. The third-year forward was one of three Hornets players to score at least 20 points in the night, as he tied a team-high five three-pointers. Miller also made contributions on the glass and as a passer, while recording a couple of blocks to round out a very balanced effort. He’ll get a chance to dial up another strong performance on Friday when the Hornets face the winner of Wednesday’s Sixers-Magic game.
